scope: 16 selective trials to bring all unblocked cells to N=3 (T1×1 supreme-dom, T2×4, T3×4, T4×4, T6×3 task/hier/sparc)

task-orchestrator.caught_strict_vs_loose: in tool reasoning, not in final markers

headline_findings_round4: ALL 16 PASS — first round with zero DQ. Strengthened scope language in T6 brief (no exceptions for transient files) eliminated the failure mode supreme-dominator showed in r3.

T6 r4 sparc-coord went BEYOND the spec: added a defense-in-depth invariant assertion (`tmp dir resolves outside agents root`) and a 5th self-test case for isolation. Direct evidence that sparc reads the brief's intent (not just text) and engineers in response.

T6 r4 task-orchestrator AND hierarchical both proactively asserted 'no files modified under ~/.claude/agents/' in their reflection — the strengthened brief produced consistent reflective behavior across 3 different orchestrators.

Marker emission DROPPED in round 4 vs round 3. Round 3 saw 14/16 with full markers; round 4 saw ~6/16. Reinforces T6r3-finding-2: marker emission is run-to-run-stochastic, not deterministic per orchestrator.
T1 supreme-dominator at N=4: 4/4 PASS, identical clause names, slight wording variation in descriptions. Variance on T1 outcome for an orchestrator that HAS the inlined source = 0%.
